paragraphs: Markets over the last day: the eight tracked equity indices moved +0.50% on average, with Hang Seng strongest (+1.79%) and Nasdaq weakest (-0.34%). Brent crude changed +1.92% to 106.73. Gold changed -0.65% to 4,188.8999. Bitcoin changed -1.25% to 82,633.3438. The US 10-year yield stands at 5.24%, a relative move of -0.08%. Among the firms tracked, Equinor (+2.72%) and TotalEnergies (+2.57%) moved the most.

Deals and capital markets: CVC sought to hush Israel defence deal to avoid controversy (FT Markets). Private equity firm made unusual decision not to announce its acquisition of a 40% stake in camouflage maker Fibrotex Deals and capital markets: Private equity puts string of UK high street names up for sale (FT World). Owners of PizzaExpress, Morrisons and Itsu seeking exits as buyout groups cool on sector Central banks and macro: Will September inflation cement US interest rate policy for the rest of the year? (FT World). Market Questions is the FT’s guide to the week ahead Geopolitics and trade: Trump faces Republican opposition to his diesel deal with Russia’s Putin (FT Markets). Lawmakers from both parties say the agreement would finance Putin’s war machine in Ukraine and violate US law Geopolitics and trade: UK imposes new sanctions on Iran over RAF Fairford incident (FT World). Andy Burnham says events at Gloucestershire base used by US military were ‘almost certainly directed’ by Islamic Revolutionary Guards
